model.name: Companies as shared scenario units
model.description: Each company is an ior:class:Company scenario unit; multiple profiles reference the SAME company unit (dedup by name) with no duplication, making Company a first-class shared entity in the object graph.
model.tronQuote: > TRON: "ior:class:Company. Multiple profiles reference SAME company unit, no duplication. Company is first-class entity in object graph."
model.architectureRef: ior:file:scrum.pmo/sprints/sprint-21-contact-identity/architecture.md#4-company-dedup-shared-scenario-units (section 4; companyNameKey algo, domain strong key, autocomplete UX, unit shape, mintOrReuseShared)

acceptanceCriteria.text: companyNameKey(raw) is deterministic and pure — identical input always yields identical output; the SAME implementation is shared by server and client.
Normalization steps, in order: NFKD unicode-fold + strip diacritics, lowercase, replace & with " and ", repeat-strip legal suffixes until stable, strip all non-alphanumerics.
Canonical collapse: "Cerulean Circle", "cerulean circle GmbH", and "CeruleanCircle" all map to nameKey "ceruleancircle".

Legal-suffix strip is token-wise, case-insensitive, repeated until stable, and covers at least: gmbh, mbh, ag, se, kg, ug, inc, llc, ltd, limited, corp, corporation, co, company, plc, lp, llp, sa, sarl, bv, nv, oy, ab, as, spa, srl, pty (so "GmbH & Co KG" fully strips).
nameKey is a RECALL/suggestion key ONLY: a nameKey collision NEVER by itself triggers an automatic merge of two companies.
When a company email or URL is available, domain = the registrable host derived from it (e.g. cerulean.circle); otherwise domain is null.
Domain is AUTHORITATIVE: two inputs with the same domain resolve to the SAME company unit even if their names (and nameKeys) differ.
Two inputs with DIFFERENT domains resolve to SEPARATE company units even if their nameKeys collide (e.g. "Apple Inc" vs an unrelated "Apple").
Where a domain is present it overrides nameKey in both lookup and mint decisions.
GET /api/company/suggest?q=<typed> returns up to 5 existing units ranked: exact nameKey > domain match > nameKey prefix > token-overlap fuzzy (Jaccard on word-set).
The suggestion list ALWAYS includes a permanent bottom row "Create \"<typed>\"".
Selecting an existing suggestion reuses that Company uuid — NO new unit is minted.
Choosing Create mints a NEW unit even if a nameKey neighbour exists (explicit user override = distinct company): no silent merge ever happens from normalization alone.
When a user confirms a typed variant onto an existing unit, the raw typed string is appended to that unit aliases[] (for future recall + audit).
The company input is debounced (~150 ms) before querying /api/company/suggest.
mintOrReuseShared(name, domain?) step 1: if domain present and alt/company-domain/<domain> exists, return that unit uuid (no mint).
Step 2: else if alt/company/<nameKey> exists, return that unit uuid (no mint).
Step 3: else mint a new ior:class:Company, declare unitLinks (nameKey + domain when known), and index.put (which self-syncs the symlinks).

Concurrent first-mint of the same nameKey does NOT create a duplicate: the alt/company/<nameKey> symlink is created with an atomic exclusive (wx) write — first writer wins, the loser re-reads the winner.
Each company is an ior:class:Company unit whose model carries: { uuid, name (display = first-entered form), nameKey, domain|null, aliases[], unitLinks[] }.
unitLinks include alt/company/<nameKey>.scenario.json and, when domain is known, alt/company-domain/<domain>.scenario.json — both symlinks point to the Company unit ITSELF (not to a profile).
Profile.model.companies[] holds the forward IOR(s) to Company unit(s); a profile may reference multiple companies.
Company.ownerIor === null — a company is owned by NO single profile (legitimate null, like a Skill unit).
Multiple profiles reference the SAME Company uuid via their own companies[]; there is exactly one unit, no duplication.

There is NO back-pointer/members[] array on Company (forward-only): "who works here" is answered by walking all profiles companies[]; any member count shown in UI is a derived read, never stored as source of truth.

testScenarios.name: normalization collapses variants
testScenarios.given: the three strings "Cerulean Circle", "cerulean circle GmbH", "CeruleanCircle"
testScenarios.then: all three return "ceruleancircle"; the function is pure (repeat calls identical)

testScenarios.name: nameKey never auto-merges
testScenarios.given: an existing company with nameKey "apple" (domain apple.com) and a user typing "Apple" with no/different domain
testScenarios.when: the user chooses Create instead of selecting the suggestion
testScenarios.then: a SECOND distinct Company unit is minted — nameKey collision alone did not merge them

testScenarios.name: domain authoritative — same
testScenarios.given: an existing company unit with domain cerulean.circle named "Cerulean Circle"
testScenarios.then: the existing uuid is returned via the domain index; no new unit minted even though the name differs

testScenarios.name: domain authoritative — distinct
testScenarios.given: two inputs "Apple" domain apple.com and "Apple" domain apple-fruitstand.de (same nameKey "apple")
testScenarios.then: TWO separate Company units exist — different domains keep them apart despite the nameKey collision

testScenarios.name: autocomplete ranking + create row
testScenarios.given: company units {Cerulean Circle, Cerulean Cloud, Circle K} and the user types "cer" (debounced)
testScenarios.then: returns ranked matches (exact/domain/prefix/fuzzy, <=5) AND a permanent row Create "cer"

testScenarios.name: select reuses, create mints, alias recorded
testScenarios.when: user A selects it from suggestions, user B types "cerulean circle gmbh" and selects the same suggestion
testScenarios.then: both reference the one uuid (no new unit); "cerulean circle gmbh" is appended to that unit aliases[]

testScenarios.name: mintOrReuseShared dedup order
testScenarios.when: mintOrReuseShared("Cerulean Circle") then mintOrReuseShared("CeruleanCircle") are called
testScenarios.then: the first mints a unit + alt/company/ceruleancircle symlink; the second returns the SAME uuid via the nameKey hit (no duplicate)

testScenarios.name: concurrent first-mint no duplicate
testScenarios.given: two profiles minting "NewCo" (nameKey newco) at the same instant
testScenarios.then: exactly ONE Company unit exists; the wx-exclusive symlink create lets the first win and the second re-reads the winner uuid

testScenarios.name: unit shape + alt symlinks
testScenarios.then: unit.model = {uuid, name:"Cerulean Circle", nameKey:"ceruleancircle", domain:"cerulean.circle", aliases:[], unitLinks:[alt/company/ceruleancircle..., alt/company-domain/cerulean.circle...]}; both symlinks resolve to THIS unit file

testScenarios.name: shared ownership, no duplication
testScenarios.given: two profiles P1, P2 both adding "Cerulean Circle"
testScenarios.then: one Company unit with ownerIor===null exists; P1.companies[] and P2.companies[] both contain the SAME company IOR; a profile may also hold a second, different company IOR

testScenarios.name: no back-pointer; members derived
testScenarios.given: a Company referenced by P1 and P2
testScenarios.when: the unit is inspected and "who works here" is queried
testScenarios.then: the Company unit has NO members[]/profiles[] field; the answer is computed by walking all profiles companies[] (P1,P2)
